group.passage: Many people have heard that no two snowflakes look exactly alike. Is this true, and if so, why? Below, a short science article explains how snowflakes form, and a photographer who takes close-up pictures of snow answers a few questions about her work.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: How a Snowflake Grows
passage_parts.text: A snowflake begins its life high in a cloud. When the air is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a bit of dust and becomes an ice crystal. As the crystal falls, more water from the air freezes onto it, and it slowly grows arms. Because of the way water freezes, almost every snow crystal has six sides or six arms. Temperature decides the basic shape. At some temperatures, the ice grows into long, thin needles; when it is much colder, it forms flat plates. Even a small change in the air, lasting only a few seconds, can change the way the arms grow. Each crystal follows its own path to the ground and meets slightly different conditions on the way down. That is why the six arms of one snowflake look alike, but two snowflakes are almost never the same.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Five Minutes with a Snow Photographer
passage_parts.text: How do you take pictures of something so small? On cold nights, I catch falling snow on a piece of dark cloth. Then I lift one snowflake with a soft brush and put it under a camera with a special lens. I have to work fast, because even my warm breath can melt it. When is the best time to work? Snow only forms when the air is cold enough, and the nicest pieces fall when it is very cold and there is almost no wind. On warm or windy days, I mostly find broken pieces. Have you ever found two that were exactly alike? Never. I have taken thousands of pictures, and each one is different. Some look like stars, and others look like tiny plates. That is what keeps me going back outside.

tags.topic: 雪花為什麼形狀都不同

1.explanation_zh: 科普短文說雪花的起點是：When the air is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a bit of dust（空氣很冷時，一小滴水在一粒灰塵上結冰）。空格前是 a tiny piece of，要填名詞；只看這一句，ice、glass 等字也說得通，但文中說水滴是凍結在灰塵上，照抄 dust 即可（不可數名詞，不加 s）。
evidence: When the air is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a bit of dust and becomes an ice crystal.
1.strategy_zh: 空格句的 drop of water、turns into ice、high in a cloud 對應 Text A 第二句；a tiny piece of ＝ a bit of，後面照抄名詞。
hints: 空格前是 a tiny piece of：要填一個名詞。
回到 Text A：水滴在雲裡凍結在什麼東西上？
原文 freezes onto a bit of ___；照抄這個名詞。

2.explanation_zh: 訪談中攝影師說 I lift one snowflake with a soft brush and put it under a camera（用軟刷挑起一片雪花，放到相機底下）。空格前是介系詞 before，後面接動名詞：put → putting（t 要重複）。
evidence: Then I lift one snowflake with a soft brush and put it under a camera with a special lens.
2.strategy_zh: 用 soft brush、camera 回到訪談的第一個回答；介系詞 before 後面的動詞改成 V-ing，注意 put 的拼法。
hints: 空格前是介系詞 before：要填動名詞（V-ing）。
回到 Text B 第一個回答：攝影師用軟刷挑起雪花之後，接著怎麼處理？
原文 and ___ it under a camera；改成 V-ing 時字尾子音要重複。

3.explanation_zh: 兩篇都支持的是 C、F。C：短文說冰晶會長成細長的針狀或扁平的板狀（flat plates），攝影師也說有的雪花像星星、有的像小板子（tiny plates）。F：短文說空氣很冷時水滴才會結冰變成冰晶，攝影師也說 Snow only forms when the air is cold enough。A 只有短文提到，B、E 只有訪談提到，D 兩篇都沒提到。
evidence: At some temperatures, the ice grows into long, thin needles; when it is much colder, it forms flat plates.
Some look like stars, and others look like tiny plates.
When the air is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a bit of dust and becomes an ice crystal.
Snow only forms when the air is cold enough, and the nicest pieces fall when it is very cold and there is almost no wind.

option_notes_zh.A: 只有 Text A 說水滴凍結在一粒灰塵上；訪談沒有提到灰塵，只符合一方。
option_notes_zh.B: 只有訪談說有風的日子多半只拍到碎片（broken pieces）；短文沒有談到風，只符合一方。
option_notes_zh.D: 兩篇都沒有比較山上和城市的雪花大小。
option_notes_zh.E: 只有攝影師說自己溫暖的呼氣就能讓雪花融化；短文沒有提到，只符合一方。

3.strategy_zh: 「兩篇都支持」題：每個選項都要在科普短文和訪談各找到一句依據；只出現在其中一篇的細節（灰塵、風、呼氣）都不選。
hints: 題目問兩篇「都」支持的敘述，只出現在一篇的不能選。
比較兩篇：雪花需要什麼天氣？雪花有哪些形狀？
兩篇都提到 cold，也都提到 plates。

A: When the air is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a bit of dust and becomes an ice crystal.
B: On warm or windy days, I mostly find broken pieces.
C: At some temperatures, the ice grows into long, thin needles; when it is much colder, it forms flat plates.
Some look like stars, and others look like tiny plates.
D: Each crystal follows its own path to the ground and meets slightly different conditions on the way down.
E: I have to work fast, because even my warm breath can melt it.
F: When the air is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a bit of dust and becomes an ice crystal.
Snow only forms when the air is cold enough, and the nicest pieces fall when it is very cold and there is almost no wind.

4.explanation_zh: 攝影師說她把雪花放到 a camera with a special lens（裝了特殊鏡頭的相機）底下。lens 是名詞，指「透鏡、鏡頭」，是能把東西放大或看清楚的彎曲玻璃片。
evidence: Then I lift one snowflake with a soft brush and put it under a camera with a special lens.
4.strategy_zh: 依英文定義找字：題目限定訪談、限定名詞；想想拍很小的東西時相機需要什麼，只寫那一個名詞。
hints: 要找一個名詞，意思是「能讓東西看起來更大或更清楚的彎曲玻璃片」。
看 Text B 第一個回答：攝影師用的是什麼樣的相機？
答案在 a camera with a special ___；寫這個名詞。

translation_zh.text:
【引言】很多人都聽說過，世界上沒有兩片雪花長得一模一樣。這是真的嗎？如果是，原因是什麼？以下一篇科普短文說明雪花怎麼形成，另一位專拍雪花特寫的攝影師則回答幾個關於她工作的問題。
【A 雪花是怎麼長成的】雪花的一生從高高的雲裡開始。空氣很冷的時候，一小滴水在一粒灰塵上結冰，變成冰晶。冰晶往下落時，空氣中更多的水在它上面結冰，它就慢慢長出「手臂」。由於水結冰的方式，幾乎每一個雪的晶體都有六個邊或六條手臂。溫度決定了基本形狀：在某些溫度下，冰會長成細長的針狀；更冷的時候，則形成扁平的板狀。空氣中即使只是持續幾秒鐘的小小變化，都能改變手臂生長的方式。每個冰晶落到地面的路徑都不一樣，一路上遇到的條件也略有不同。所以，同一片雪花的六條手臂看起來很像，但兩片雪花幾乎從來不會一模一樣。
【B 雪花攝影師五分鐘訪談】問：這麼小的東西，您怎麼拍？答：在寒冷的夜晚，我用一塊深色的布接住落下的雪。然後用軟刷挑起一片雪花，放到裝了特殊鏡頭的相機底下。我的動作要很快，因為就連我溫暖的呼氣都可能讓它融化。問：什麼時候最適合工作？答：空氣夠冷才會下雪，而最漂亮的雪花會在非常冷、幾乎沒有風的時候落下。天氣暖或風大的日子，我拍到的大多是碎片。問：您有沒有找到過兩片一模一樣的雪花？答：從來沒有。我拍過好幾千張照片，每一片都不同。有的像星星，有的像小小的板子。正是這一點，讓我一次又一次回到戶外。
